title: Reasoning or Pattern Exploitation? Mechanistic Insights from RL-Trained Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2610.39182v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly described as acquiring "reasoning" skills after reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards. However, whether these gains reflect genuine reasoning or more superficial adaptations remains underexplored. In this work, we probe LLMs trained in a finite and exhaustively analyzable logical domain, namely Tic-Tac-Toe, and trace how internal representations evolve across reinforcement learning (RL) with Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO). Quantitatively, RL yields high accuracy and robustness across prompt variations, suggesting the emergence of game reasoning. Mechanistic interpretability, however, paints a different picture: features extracted with sparse autoencoders (SAEs) reveal that models primarily adapt to rely more heavily on information already explicit in the prompt, such as whose turn it is, game progression and board occupancy. translated_title: 推理还是模式利用？来自强化学习训练语言模型的机制性洞察
translated_abstract: 大语言模型（LLM）在经过可验证奖励的强化学习后，越来越被描述为获得了“推理”能力。然而，这些能力提升究竟反映了真正的推理，还是更为表面的适应性调整，目前仍缺乏充分探究。在本工作中，我们在一个有限且可穷尽分析的逻辑领域——井字棋——中探究语言模型，并追踪其内部表征在采用组相对策略优化（GRPO）的强化学习（RL）过程中如何演变。定量结果表明，RL 在各种提示变体下均带来了高准确率和鲁棒性，似乎暗示了博弈推理能力的出现。然而，机制可解释性分析却呈现出不同的图景：通过稀疏自编码器（SAE）提取的特征显示，模型主要适应于更依赖提示中已经明确给出的信息，例如轮到谁走棋、游戏进程以及棋盘占用情况。相比之下，像棋盘对称性这样的高级概念……
tldr: 本研究通过在井字棋领域进行机制可解释性分析发现，强化学习训练后的语言模型表面上展现的“推理”能力，实际上主要源于对提示中已有显式信息的依赖，而非真正的推理能力。
en_tdlr: Through mechanistic interpretability in the finite game of Tic-Tac-Toe, this study reveals that apparent reasoning gains in RL-trained language models largely stem from exploiting information already explicit in the prompt rather than genuine reasoning ability.
